Equation (7), page 4, gives a Lambert-W asymptotic approximation for the nth positive order zero at fixed z>0. Section 2 derives its classical action and WKB quantization approximation.
limitations: The Bohr–Sommerfeld relation in Section 2 is a semiclassical input, not an exact eigenvalue equation.
Numerical claims and the full claimed remainder in equation (7) have not been independently verified.
This does not identify individual Riemann zeta zeros.
research_questions: Compare exact gamma-phase counting with the WKB action while preserving all normalization factors.
Use the solvable positive kernel to test which spectral/Laplace assumptions fail to enforce an all-zero conclusion.

title: On the Riemann Hypothesis in Function-Fields
version: original journal pages 345–347, assembled from PMC page scans
read_scope: Read all three article pages, following the intersection numbers, positive form, Frobenius power sums, and real interpolation contradiction. The note defers full foundational details of the correspondence theory.
source_locator: pp. 345–347, especially the polynomial argument on p. 347
main_result: For a separable one-variable function field over F_q in Weil's setup, positivity of the correspondence trace pairing and reciprocal pairing of eigenvalues imply that all reciprocal roots have absolute value √q.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The proof uses the Frobenius correspondence and its transpose, with product q times the identity, on a smooth projective curve. No correspondence with these properties is available here for the completed classical zeta function.

title: Sur les courbes algébriques et les variétés qui s’en déduisent
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at § IV, no. 22.
main_result: The zeta-function numerator of the curve has roots on the circle abs(u)=q^(-1/2), by the preceding theory of correspondences.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The argument uses the polarization of a curve's Jacobian and the evaluation of point counts through Frobenius iterates over finite fields.

title: Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles
read_scope: Read §§1–4 and the conclusion, following Dwork–Faton's trace criterion, diagonal projectors, the equivalence argument via X×X, and the conditional positivity implication.
main_result: Formulates C(X), A(X)/B(X) and Hdg(X). B(X) and Hdg(X×X) imply the Weil weight assertion for endomorphisms scaling the polarization by q, and hence its Frobenius case.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Even the conditional argument requires an algebraic Lefschetz operator and a positive primitive intersection form for an appropriate geometric realization. The paper supplies these as conjectures about varieties.

title: Some consequences of the Riemann hypothesis for varieties over finite fields
version: original journal PDF with archive cover sheet
read_scope: Read all five printed pages from the scan and OCR, including the Lefschetz pencil divisibility proof, hard Lefschetz corollary, and polynomial construction of cycle projectors.
source_locator: § II Theorem 1 and Corollary 1, § III Theorem 2
main_result: For smooth projective geometrically irreducible varieties over F_q, any cohomology satisfying the stated duality, weak Lefschetz and zeta formula has the étale Frobenius polynomials. With the extra cycle-class hypothesis, Künneth projectors are rational combinations of Frobenius graphs.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The comparison starts with Deligne's established weight-stratified Frobenius polynomials and an alternating cohomological factorization. Neither input is furnished for classical ζ.

title: The Selberg trace formula for groups of F-rank one
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §3 Assumption 3.5 and Theorem 3.6, §9.
main_result: For the adelic F-rank-one setup the discrete automorphic convolution operator is trace class under Assumption 3.5 (K-finite convolution factors and the prescribed vanishing on almost all ramified classes), and §9 gives the trace expansion after continuous and geometric divergences cancel.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The trace class statement concerns the discrete automorphic convolution operator; its spectrum and the parabolic correction terms give no operator whose eigenvalues are all classical zeta zeros.

title: A trace formula for reductive groups I. Terms associated to classes in G(Q)
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §7 Theorem 7.1 and §8.
main_result: For sufficiently regular truncation parameter T the sum of integrals of the absolute values of the class kernels is finite. The resulting geometric distributions are indexed by rational conjugacy of semisimple parts.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: This is geometric control of a truncated reductive-group automorphic kernel. It does not identify an untruncated self-adjoint operator with classical ζ's explicit formula.

title: L-indistinguishability for SL(2)
version: IAS typeset copy of published article
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §§6–7, Propositions 7.2–7.4.
main_result: Computes global automorphic multiplicities for SL(2) and its inner forms by distinguishing packet types and tracking contributions related to tori.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Packet multiplicities are for automorphic representations on a prescribed group. Stabilizing this trace formula yields no zero-location theorem for the degree-one trivial Hecke L-function.

title: Gauss Sums, Kloosterman Sums, and Monodromy Groups
venue: Annals of Mathematics Studies 116, Princeton University Press
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Chapter 11, §§11.1, 11.4.
main_result: Determines geometric monodromy of rank n≥2 Kloosterman sheaves: Sp(n) for even n, SL(n) for odd n and odd p, SO(n) for odd n≠7 and p=2, and G₂ for n=7 and p=2. §11.4 applies equidistribution to the normalized Frobenius classes.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: These compact laws use the computed monodromy of a pure finite-field sheaf. They do not construct a sheaf giving classical zeta zeros.

title: Random matrices, Frobenius eigenvalues, and monodromy
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §§9.2 and 9.6, especially Theorems 9.2.6 and 9.6.10.
main_result: Equidistribution theorems for unitarized Frobenius in pure lisse families, including uniform control in §9.6, support the separate normalized spacing limits of Chapter 1.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The proof needs purity and finite-field averaging plus explicit geometric monodromy. Even an agreement of spacing limits would not rule out exceptional zeros of a single classical function.

title: Zeroes of zeta functions and symmetry
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §3 and §4, equation (30) and the analogy table.
source_locator: §3 and §4, equation (30) and the analogy table
main_result: Explains how Frobenius on curve cohomology gives a unitary conjugacy class and how symplectic monodromy for suitable curve families yields the corresponding family statistics.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The spectral interpretation in §3 depends on curve cohomology. Quantum-chaos or compact-group statistical similarity does not identify a classical ζ spectral operator.

title: Functoriality for the classical groups
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §1 Theorem 1.1.
main_result: Irreducible globally generic cuspidal representations for the paper's split classical groups over number fields admit the specified functorial lifts to GL(N).
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Functoriality identifies local parameters and analytic L-functions. It imposes no all-zero constraint for ζ, whose GL(1) realization is already known.

title: Le lemme fondamental pour les algèbres de Lie
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1.11.1, support Theorem 7.6.6 and proof §8.6 in arXiv v3.
source_locator: Theorem 1.11.1, support Theorem 7.6.6 and proof §8.6 in arXiv v3
main_result: The Lie-algebra fundamental lemma matches stable and weighted-by-character orbital integrals for corresponding endoscopic data, using geometric stabilization and the Hitchin fibration, under the stated local characteristic bounds.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The identities concern endoscopic orbital integrals. The Hitchin cohomology supplies Frobenius traces for that comparison, without realizing the completed classical ζ function.

title: The subconvexity problem for GL2
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §1 Theorems 1.1 and 1.2.
main_result: An absolute δ>0 gives C^(1/4−δ) central-value bounds for GL(1), GL(2) with unitary central character and the stated GL(2)×GL(2) Rankin–Selberg family with one representation fixed; imaginary twists include t-aspect.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The method gives quantitative upper bounds for values. Such a bound lacks the zero exclusion needed in Re s>1/2 for ζ.

title: Galois representations arising from some compact Shimura varieties
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1.2, assembled from Theorems 7.5, 7.11 and Corollary 7.13.
source_locator: Theorem 1.2, assembled from Theorems 7.5, 7.11 and Corollary 7.13
main_result: For regular algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal GL(m) over CM fields with the stated slight regularity for even m, constructs semisimple ℓ-adic Galois representations realizing local parameters away from ℓ.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: These Galois representations realize individual local parameters. Their existence gives no global Frobenius operator whose spectrum lists the classical ζ zeros.

title: The fundamental lemma of Jacquet and Rallis
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Introduction, Main Theorem (Local part), Corollary, and Appendix Theorem A.1.
source_locator: Introduction, Main Theorem (Local part), Corollary, and Appendix Theorem A.1
main_result: In equal characteristic >n, the local theorem identifies the specified graded Frobenius modules for matching invariants with trivial η on the discriminant. The corollary yields the Jacquet–Rallis orbital-integral identity, and Gordon's transfer gives large-residue-characteristic cases.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The matched distributions are those of the relative trace formula over local fields. Transfer of local identities does not pass a finite-field Weil bound to classical ζ.

title: The mean value of L(1/2, χ) in the hyperelliptic ensemble
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §2, Theorem 1 and equation (2.5).
main_result: For fixed q≡1 mod 4, obtains the first moment of L(1/2,χ_D) over monic squarefree D of degree 2g+1, with Euler-product main and secondary terms and power-saving error.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The degree truncation from the curve L-polynomial, averaging over D and finite-field character cancellation are unavailable for a single classical ζ.

title: The Variance of the Number of Prime Polynomials in Short Intervals and in Residue Classes
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §2, Theorems 2.1 and 2.2.
main_result: At fixed h<n−3, q^(−h−1) times the short interval variance tends to n−h−2 as q→∞. The progression theorem gives G(n;Q)∼q^n(deg Q−1) for fixed n≥2, Q squarefree and n≥deg Q−1.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The varying-field limit uses matrix trace averages from finite-field equidistribution. Its integer analogue involves a separate limit tied to ζ pair correlation.

title: Hardy–Littlewood Tuple Conjecture over Large Finite Fields
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1.1.
main_result: For fixed n,r and odd prime power q, the number of monic degree-n f with all f+a_i irreducible for distinct shifts of degree<n is q^n/n^r+O_(n,r)(q^(n−1/2)).
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The bound uses geometric monodromy over coefficient space and finite-field Chebotarev with q→∞ at fixed degree. Integer primes do not vary over that coefficient space.

title: Conjectures for the integral moments and ratios of L-functions over function fields
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §5, Conjecture 5 and Theorem 1, equation (5.29).
main_result: Derives the predicted leading kth hyperelliptic moment conditional on Conjecture 5, with logarithmic exponent k(k+1)/2 and explicit arithmetic factor.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The moment formula is a conditional family prediction, so it provides neither an all-zero constraint nor a mechanism for changing the family or base field.

title: Witt Vectors and a Question of Rudnick and Waxman
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §5 Theorem 5.1.
main_result: For odd n≥7 and field sizes tending to infinity, primitive super-even Witt-vector characters have normalized Frobenius classes equidistributed in USp(n−1), allowing varying characteristic. The n=3,5 clauses restrict characteristics.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The symmetry group arises from Witt-vector character sheaves and controls family sampling. The construction gives no classical ζ Frobenius class.

title: The fourth moment of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions over function fields
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1.1 and Appendix (9.19)–(9.21).
main_result: For prime q≡1 mod 4, the fourth central moment over monic squarefree degree 2g+1 is q^(2g+1) times an explicit degree-10 polynomial truncated through g^8, with error O(q^(2g+1)g^(15/2+ε)).
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Polynomial Poisson summation and exact finite degree cutoffs control this quadratic family. Its arithmetic and asymptotic scale differ from the t-aspect fourth moment of ζ.

title: Shtukas and the Taylor expansion of L-functions
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, proof §9.3.2.
main_result: For an everywhere unramified cuspidal representation of PGL(2) over the function field, the normalized even rth derivative at 1/2 of the quadratic base-change L-function equals the self-intersection of its projected Heegner–Drinfeld cycle.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: This is a special-value identity for a base-change L-function on a moduli stack of shtukas. An identity at the center does not give the signs or spectral data for all classical ζ zeros.

title: The equidistribution of L-functions of twists by Witt vector Dirichlet characters over function fields
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1.1.
main_result: For pairwise twist-inequivalent cuspidal GL(m_i) representations with finite-order central characters and no nontrivial degree self-twist, most Witt twists admit normalized unitary conjugacy classes, which jointly equidistribute in the determinant-normalized sense of the theorem for d≥4.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The asymptotic is finite-field extension at fixed conductor exponent, via sheaf Fourier transforms and monodromy. It does not control zeros of classical ζ.

title: Twisted moments of L-functions and spectral reciprocity
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1, equations (1.8)–(1.9).
main_result: For admissible h, coprime q,ℓ, 1/2≤Re s≤Re w<3/4 and fixed GL(3) cusp form or minimal Eisenstein series, relates the twisted moment at level q to moments at level ℓ plus a main term.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Reciprocity exchanges level and twist in an averaged spectral moment. The identity imposes no spectral-location constraint on ζ.

title: Motohashi’s fourth moment identity for non-archimedean test functions and applications
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1, equations (1.14)–(1.15).
main_result: For prime q, coprime squarefree comparable twists a,b prime to q and the specified holomorphic Schwartz weight and shift strip, relates the twisted character moment and trivial term to a polar term and spectral moment.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The non-archimedean test function organizes a moment over Dirichlet characters and a Maaß spectral sum. Neither side expresses the full classical ζ zero set.

title: A representation theory approach to integral moments of L-functions over function fields
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Hypothesis H and Theorem 1.4, equation (1.2).
main_result: Under H(n,r,r̃,w), n>2max(r,r̃)+1, and characteristic different from 2 when n=4 or 5, evaluates the shifted twisted moment over primitive even characters up to the stated geometric error.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The key vanishing statement is a hypothesis on geometric cohomology of a conductor-controlled family, with no established classical ζ analogue.

title: On the Ramanujan conjecture for automorphic forms over function fields I. Geometry
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1.1 and Condition BC.
main_result: For a split semisimple group over a function field of characteristic >2, with a monomial geometric supercuspidal local component and base-changeability, proves temperedness at unramified places.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Temperedness controls local Satake parameters. For ζ these local parameters are elementary already, and a bound on their moduli does not locate global zeros.

title: Symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic modular forms, II
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem A.
main_result: All positive symmetric powers of a regular algebraic non-CM cuspidal GL(2) representation over Q exist as regular algebraic cuspidal GL(n+1) representations.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Symmetric power automorphy gives continuation and functional equations of different higher-rank L-functions. It adds no global zero exclusion for the trivial GL(1) L-function.

title: On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over F_q[T]
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorems 1.1 and 1.3.
main_result: At fixed q=p^a>685090p², p odd, and nonzero h, proves the monic twin prime asymptotic with a power saving as degree grows. The Chowla statement has its separately stated q and shift conditions.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The fixed-q limit uses geometric character sum estimates and polynomial factorization. It is a distinct prime-counting problem from integer prime correlations, let alone all zeros of ζ.

title: Geometrization of the local Langlands correspondence
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at § I.9 Theorem I.9.6 and § I.10 Theorem I.10.1.
source_locator: § I.9 Theorem I.9.6 and § I.10 Theorem I.10.1
main_result: Constructs local L-parameters for irreducible smooth representations and proves compatibility properties including tori, parabolic induction and supercuspidal GL(n). Theorem I.10.1 treats a spectral action subject to the stated ℓ condition.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: This is local geometry over a nonarchimedean field. The parameterization does not produce a global operator with the archimedean factor and zero spectrum of ζ.

title: Étale and crystalline companions, II
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorems 0.1.1 and 0.1.2, Corollaries 8.1.5 and 8.1.7.
main_result: On a smooth scheme over a finite field, an irreducible coefficient with finite-order determinant is pure of weight 0 and admits companions including at p. Algebraic coefficients admit companions at the stated primes more generally.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Companion comparison preserves characteristic polynomials of closed-point Frobenius in existing finite-field cohomology. It has no input realizing classical ζ across all rational primes.

title: Proof of the geometric Langlands conjecture V: the multiplicity one theorem
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Introduction equation (0.1), Theorems 4.3.2 and 5.2.3.
main_result: Completes the geometric Langlands equivalence for the de Rham categories in the series. The argument uses scalar endomorphisms of the vacuum Poincaré sheaf and the indicated topology of irreducible local systems.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The geometric categorical equivalence for bundles and local systems on a curve does not identify the completed classical ζ function or certify real spectral parameters for its zeros.

title: Spectral moment formulae for GL(3) × GL(2) L-functions I: The cuspidal case
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at §1B Theorems 1.1 and 1.2.
main_result: For a fixed Hecke-normalized spherical SL(3,Z) Maaß cusp form with imaginary Langlands parameters and H in Cη, for 1/4+1/200<Re s<3/4 gives a weighted GL(3)×GL(2) spectral first-moment identity with integral transforms; Theorem 1.2 gives an identity for the transform when 1/2+1/100<Re s<1.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The cusp form is fixed and the degree-six L-functions are averaged over SL(2,Z) spectrum. This is not an eigenvalue identity for ζ.

title: Spectral moment formulae for GL(3) × GL(2) L-functions III: the twisted case
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1.1, equation (1.4).
main_result: An admissible weight H and 1/4+1/200<Re s<3/4 give a reciprocity formula for the Hecke-twisted GL(3)×GL(2) first moment, with continuous and explicit arithmetic terms.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The formula analyzes a Hecke-twisted average and its transforms. It carries no sign or vanishing implication for individual classical ζ zeros.

title: Spectral moment formulae for GL(3) × GL(2) L-functions II: the Eisenstein case
venue: Journal of the Institute of Mathematics of Jussieu 25, 2265–2312
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorems 1.3–1.5, especially (1.7).
main_result: For H in Cη and 1/4+ε₀<Re s<3/4 establishes the explicit Eisenstein spectral reciprocity identity with residue terms and zeta-product integral; the central specialization is in Theorem 1.5.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The identity does contain ζ-products, but as shifted moments integrated against a transform. It gives no positivity condition forcing each zero onto the line.

title: Nonvanishing of L-functions associated to fixed order characters over function fields
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2.
main_result: For ℓ≥3, q fixed with q≡1 mod 2ℓ, and d nonzero modulo ℓ, obtains one-level density for the specified thin family with Fourier support depending on ℓ (6/5 for ℓ=3 and 26/23 for ℓ=4) and proves positive-proportion central nonvanishing.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The argument starts from the function-field RH and bounds an average over residue-symbol characters. A central nonvanishing frequency does not constrain off-line zeros of ζ.

title: Short sums of trace functions over function fields and their applications
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1.3 and four preceding sheaf assumptions.
source_locator: Theorem 1.3 and four preceding sheaf assumptions
main_result: For the stated sheaves over squarefree moduli, bounds the sum over polynomials of norm <X by √q X^(1/2)Norm(g)^(log_q(2r(t)+c(t))). Each sheaf is mixed of nonpositive weights, has no finitely supported sections, has no geometric Artin–Schreier factor of the specified linear form (including the trivial factor), and has slopes at infinity at most 1.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The square-root mechanism uses geometric trace functions over the polynomial interval and conductor-dependent rank bounds. There is no supplied integer or classical ζ replacement for that geometry.

title: Symmetric power functoriality for Hilbert modular forms
version: Cambridge repository manuscript with internal pagination
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem A.
main_result: For totally real F and non-CM cuspidal GL(2) representations essentially square-integrable at infinity, each Sym^(n−1), n≥2, is cuspidal automorphic and realizes the symmetric power of the local Weil–Deligne representation at every place.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: Matching local symmetric powers for holomorphic Hilbert forms cannot give a zero-exclusion result for degree-one ζ.

title: A refined random matrix model for function field L-functions
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorems 1.2, 1.3 and 1.5.
main_result: For q>11, Theorem 1.5 compares shifted critical-line mixed moments of fixed-conductor characters over F_q[T] to the refined model moments with an explicit power error. Theorems 1.2–1.3 control complementary test components.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The comparison fixes q and increases conductor degree, preserving arithmetic corrections of a finite-field family. It does not yield an identity for the zero set of a single classical function.

title: Non-vanishing of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic L-functions
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, family (1.2).
main_result: For ℓ=3,4,6 and fixed odd q≡−1 mod ℓ, gives a positive liminf for central nonvanishing within the specified primitive non-Kummer families along ℓ−1 dividing g; Theorem 1.2 gives twisted first moments for ℓ=4,6.
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: The proof uses special finite-field families and studies values at 1/2. No passage to an all-zero assertion for classical ζ follows.

title: Bounds for standard L-functions
read_scope: Targeted reading of the primary text at Theorem 1.1, equation (1.2).
main_result: For every n there is positive t-aspect subconvex saving for unitary cuspidal GL(n) over Q, and for n≥2 the explicit lower bound for δ_n is 2/(3n^5−2n^4−n²).
classical_zeta_transfer_obstacle: A saving in the growth exponent of central-line values cannot by itself exclude a zero with real part >1/2, including for degree one.

title: A strengthening of the Nyman–Beurling criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
version: 2003 Lincei journal scan, pp. 5–11, with two BDIM front sheets
read_scope: Complete pinned journal, seven article pages, independently reconstructed by two agents and director. The integer criterion, corollary and RH-conditional rate survive local normalization/range/tail repairs and the separately established shrinking-gap supplement. The May and February deposits retain distinct manifestations and original reading scopes.
publication_status: published; original BDIM journal scan inspected
main_result: Journal Theorem 1 (p5, proof pp6–9): in H=L²(0,infinity), RH iff chi=1_(0,1] belongs to the closure of the span of rho_n(x)={1/(nx)} for every integer n≥1. Journal Theorem 2 (pp9–10), the same result as expanded May Proposition3.1: under RH, for some fixed c>0 the damped Möbius approximants with exponent c/loglog n have norm error O((loglog n)^(−1/3)).
proof_architecture: RH plus Balazard–Saias truncated Möbius estimate
Mellin transform of fractional part is -zeta(s)/s in 0<Re(s)<1
Functional-equation ratio bound Lemma2.2
H convergence n→infinity for fixed sufficiently small epsilon
H convergence epsilon↓0 to -chi, then closure
limitations: All positive integer dilations including 1 are required.
Norm limits are ordered; unconditional analytic-kernel convergence does not identify the actual damped functions off RH.
The particular printed majorant needs epsilon<1/4; a free subpower exponent proves the fixed weighted range epsilon<1/2.
Uniform shrinking-gap constants require the reconstructed supplement; no practical onset or optimality claimed.
historical_importance: Reduces continuous dilation parameters to integer dilations; turns an abstract closure criterion into arithmetic approximation.
reusable_lemma: Journal Lemma 2 (pp6–7), expanded May Lemma2.2 and February Lemma2.2 with a version-specific gamma typo: the symmetric zeta quotient has modulus at most C_(epsilon0)(1+|t|)^epsilon for 0≤epsilon≤epsilon0<1/2, by the functional equation and uniform Stirling, with removable common zero values.
research_questions: Can a quantitative uniform error bound replace the sequential limiting argument?
Which smoothing schemes preserve norm convergence with a useful explicit rate?

title: A lower bound in an approximation problem involving the zeros of the Riemann zeta function
read_scope: Complete 17 printed-page preprint read; polynomial jet-projection method reconstructed; zeta invariant-operator lemmas read but not independently rebuilt.
main_result: For B_lambda=span{{theta/t}:lambda<=theta<=1} in L²((0,infinity),dt), D(lambda)=dist(chi,B_lambda), liminf_{lambda↓0}D(lambda)*sqrt(log(1/lambda)) >= sqrt(sum_rho m_rho²/|rho|²) (Theorem1.3 p.4; Theorem5.5 pp.15–16). Proof assumes RH, since its failure makes the left side infinite; rho are distinct nontrivial zeros under that assumption. Polynomial analogue Theorem1.4: Q of positive degree with all roots alpha on the unit circle, multiplicities m_alpha, and fixed target polynomial P gives lim N inf_deg A<=N ||P-QA||²=sum_alpha m_alpha²|P(alpha)|².
proof_architecture: Finite-dimensional prediction error and jet evaluation Gram matrices (§2)
Mellin invariant unitary phase operator V (§3)
Boundary-limit Hilbert vectors Y_(s,k)^lambda and orthogonality to contracted zeta model (§4)
Rescale by log(1/lambda)^(-k-1/2)
Fixed finite set of zeros gives Cauchy Gram blocks, whose inverse top-left entries are m²
Take lower bound for every finite zero set; then increase the finite set
limitations: A lower bound only; no upper bound or complete spectral construction follows.
Fixed finite-set Gram limits do not justify a uniform infinite-set limit.
The conjectural disappearance of the continuous quotient component is explicitly speculative.
D(lambda) allows continuous dilation parameters; discrete Dirichlet-polynomial distance is at least as large at lambda=1/N.
historical_importance: Identifies multiplicity squared, not multiplicity, as the approximation obstruction; converts zero jets to asymptotic Gram blocks.
reusable_lemma: Theorem5.3: distinct fixed zeros have asymptotically vanishing cross Gram entries after scaling; same-zero derivative jets give 1/(k+l+1).
research_questions: Obtain uniform Gram estimates when zero separations shrink with the cutoff.
Control any orthogonal complement beyond the constructed zero jets before asserting a matching upper bound.

title: An optimal choice of Dirichlet polynomials for the Nyman-Beurling criterion
read_scope: Complete nine-page preprint read; hypotheses and residue proof architecture extracted; central contour estimates inspected, not all independently verified.
venue: Proceedings of the Steklov Institute of Mathematics, 2013; preprint version inspected
main_result: Assume RH and sum_{|Im rho|<=T}|zeta'(rho)|^(-2)<<T^(3/2-delta) for some delta>0. For V_N(s)=sum_{n<=N}(1-log n/log N)mu(n)n^(-s), N>1, its squared weighted critical-line error (1/(2pi))integral_R |1-zeta(1/2+it)V_N(1/2+it)|² dt/(1/4+t²) is asymptotic to (2+gamma-log(4pi))/log N (Theorem1,p.2). Moment hypothesis forces simple zeros. Theorem2,p.3: analogous triangular reciprocal Taylor window is asymptotically optimal for polynomials with simple roots on/outside the circle, if boundary roots are present.
proof_architecture: Perron representation of logarithmically weighted Möbius polynomial
Residues at pole s, nontrivial zeros, and trivial zeros (Lemma2)
Reciprocal derivative moment controls sums of zero residues (Lemma3)
Shift norm contour off critical line
Double pole residue supplies sum 1/|rho|² log N; remaining integrals are lower order
limitations: RH alone is not the theorem hypothesis.
Inverse derivative moment excludes multiplicities.
Infinite-zero residue tails require the additional moment estimate.
No finite-N inequality of the form d_N²>=C/log N is proved.
Polynomial theorem with no boundary roots should be read as o(1/N), rather than literal asymptotic equivalence to zero.
historical_importance: Under an explicit strong arithmetic hypothesis, a concrete logarithmic Möbius smoothing attains Burnol’s asymptotic lower constant.
reusable_lemma: Lemma3 pp.6–7 supplies a bound on the sum of zero-residue terms on Re(s)=1/2±epsilon using the negative derivative moment.
research_questions: Can collective residue cancellation weaken the exponent 3/2-delta?
Which estimates replace inverse simple derivatives for higher principal parts?

main_results.statement: For a nontrivial multiplicative character χ and nontrivial additive character ψ of Fq, the Gauss sum has squared absolute value q.

For ai∈Fq* and positive ni, the number N of affine solutions of Σ(i=0..r) ai xi^ni=0 satisfies |N−q^r|≤M(q−1)q^((r−1)/2), with M the number of rational tuples 0<αi<1, ni αi∈Z, Σαi∈Z. The actual character sum is restricted by di=gcd(ni,q−1); the stated M is a q-independent upper bound.
For degree-v finite-field extension, lifted characters χ′=χ∘Norm and ψ′=ψ∘Trace satisfy −G(χ′,ψ′)=(−G(χ,ψ))^v.

Diagonal projective examples yield rational generating functions with eigenvalue magnitudes matching their expected weights. The general higher-dimensional statements on p. 507 are explicitly conjectural in this paper.

definitions: Multiplicative and additive characters; gcd di=gcd(ni,q−1).
Source Jacobi sum j(α), defined for nonzero character exponents summing to zero modulo 1.
Extension-field norm/trace; generating series of point counts; conjectural Betti factors.

Reduce nonzero character contributions to Jacobi sums.
Evaluate Gauss-sum norms and express Jacobi sums as products divided by q.
Use norm/trace lift and a formal Euler product of monic polynomials to compare extensions.
Pass from homogeneous affine counts to projective counts; infer diagonal zeta weights; formulate general conjectures.

Smooth proper/projective hypotheses must be explicit in modern restatement; open A1/Gm refute unrestricted proper-curve factorization.
Square-root Gauss cancellation does not constitute a general cohomological purity proof.
No implication to classical RH is established.

main_results.statement: For X0 smooth projective over Fq and ℓ≠char Fq, det(tI−F | H^i_et(X0×Fq Fqbar,Qℓ)) has integer coefficients independent of ℓ, and all complex conjugates of its roots have magnitude q^(i/2). F is geometric Frobenius, identified with pullback of the geometric Frobenius morphism by (1.15).

For a lisse Qℓ-sheaf F0 on U0=P1/Fq minus finitely many points: a perfect alternating pairing F0⊗F0→Qℓ(−β), β∈Z; open geometric monodromy image in the corresponding Sp; and rational local characteristic polynomials at every closed point imply pointwise purity of weight β.

A middle-degree bound q^(d/2−1/2)≤|α|≤q^(d/2+1/2) for smooth projective absolutely irreducible even-dimensional varieties is amplified on even cartesian powers, using Künneth, to exact magnitude q^(d/2).

definitions: Geometric Frobenius versus inverse arithmetic Frobenius, (1.15).
Weight β at closed x means all conjugates have magnitude |k(x)|^(β/2).
Vanishing-cycle quotient E/(E∩Eperp), not an assumed nondegenerate E.
proof_architecture: Grothendieck compact-support trace/determinant formula and Poincaré duality.
Even tensor powers have positive rational local Euler coefficients; monodromy invariant theory restricts global poles.
Lefschetz pencils supply vanishing cycles and open symplectic monodromy, (5.10).
Rationality (6.2) on the nondegenerate quotient verifies the third hypothesis of (3.2).
Leray filtration yields the weak middle-degree bound (7.1).
Künneth and powers (7.3) remove a uniform ±1/2 exponent loss.
Weak Lefschetz and duality reduce arbitrary degrees to the middle degree; weight separation yields integrality and ℓ-independence.
limitations: No proof for Spec Z/classical ζ is given.
The main theorem here is projective smooth; proper smooth is the later WeilII(3.3.9).
Bilinear self-duality and positive Euler coefficients alone do not imply purity.
The entire main proof and all external SGA dependencies were not audited here.

main_results.statement: For f:X→Y between separated noetherian algebraic spaces of finite type over Z on which fixed ℓ is invertible, and a constructible Qℓbar-sheaf F mixed of weights ≤n, R^i f! F is mixed of weights ≤n+i. The paper calls these algebraic spaces schemes by convention.

For finite-type X0/Fq and mixed F0 of weights ≤n, Hc^i(X,F) has weights ≤n+i. For X0 smooth and F0 lisse of weights ≥n, H^i has weights ≥n+i. If F0 is pure weight n and lisse, im(Hc^i→H^i) is pure weight n+i.
For X0 smooth proper over Fq and ℓ≠char Fq, det(tI−F | H^i_et(X,Qℓ)) is integral and ℓ-independent, with all eigenvalue conjugates of magnitude q^(i/2). This extends I(1.6) from projective to proper.
For X0/Fq a smooth curve and F0 lisse and iota-pure of weight β, each α on Hc^1(X,F) has wq(α)<β+2, where wq(α)=2log_q|iota(α)|.

For X smooth projective pure dimension n over an algebraically closed field of characteristic ≠ℓ, and ample invertible sheaf L with η=c1(L), η^i:H^(n−i)(X,Qℓ)→H^(n+i)(X,Qℓ)(i) is an isomorphism for i≥0. The source chooses a Tate-twist trivialization in this section and suppresses twists.

definitions: Pure number of weight n relative q: algebraic and every complex conjugate has magnitude q^(n/2).
Mixed sheaf: finite filtration with pointwise pure quotients; weights are those nonzero quotient weights.
iota-purity for a chosen field isomorphism Qℓbar→C; real weights allowed.
Compact versus ordinary cohomology; image of the natural map; weight shift and Tate twist.

Purity of im(Hc→H) must not be inflated to purity of all ordinary or compact cohomology on open varieties.

version: Original 1926 article; first and last signatures printed March1926; no exact issue date inferred

main_result: Equation(7), p306: G(z;a)=∫R exp[−a(e^u+e^(−u))+zu]du, a>0, i.e. 2K_z(2a). Sections1–3 prove every zero simple and purely imaginary. proof_architecture: Integration by parts gives difference equation(9), p307.
Gamma expansion(11), pp307–308 yields asymptotic control and initial small-a zero confinement in Section2.
Zero exclusion on Re(z)=±1 follows from the recurrence, conjugation and impossible indefinitely shifted zeros, Section3 IV.
Parameter continuation in a excludes outside-strip zeros, Section3 V.
Argument-principle rectangles and phase control force no nonimaginary zeros and no excess multiplicity, Section3 VI, pp313–315.

HilfssatzI, pp315–316: a first nonzero odd derivative at zero produces an eventual fixed-sign algebraic cosine-transform tail; naive nonsymmetric finite xi-kernel truncations consequently have only finitely many real zeros.
HilfssatzII, pp316–317: symmetric imaginary shifts preserve real zeros for real entire genus0/1 functions with all zeros real and at least one zero; this gives real zeros for the symmetrized fake xi.

Original formulas were read but the entire original 1926 technical proof is not claimed independently verified.

title: On the estimate M(x)=o(x) for Beurling generalized numbers

main_result: A positive generalized integer density and a Chebyshev upper bound for the generalized primes suffice for M(x)=o(x). Theorems 2.1 and 2.3 treat multiplicative measures through a compact-uniform boundary asymptotic plus stated convolution hypotheses.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §§1–2, Corollaries 1.2 and 2.2, Theorem 2.3
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Shows what would be needed to transport pretentious mean-value control off N. Positivity/density and compact-uniform transform information are additional to the Euler-product identity, and the boundary is Re s=1, not the critical-line energy norm.
title: Halász's theorem for Beurling generalized numbers

comparison_manifestation.read_scope: Remark 2.3, equation (2.15), corrected logarithmic density normalization.

main_result: For discrete Beurling systems with π(x)≪x/log x and N(x)∼ax, counts of integers with Ω(n)≡c mod K are asymptotic to ax/K for fixed K≥2 and c. Remark 2.2 supplies the distinct-prime variant.
read_scope: Complete pinned edition. Whole PDF pp. 1–5, Theorem 1.1, Lemma 2.1 and Remark 2.2
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Finite root-of-unity filters distinguish a genuine fixed-character arithmetic averaging theorem from the prime-torus limit of derivative-weighted zero samples. Neither a growing K nor a statement about zero phases follows from this fixed K theorem.
source_locator: Whole PDF pp. 1–5, Theorem 1.1, Lemma 2.1 and Remark 2.2
title: Beurling numbers whose number of prime factors lies in a specified residue class

main_result: Super-logarithmic PNT remainders π(x)=Li(x)+O_n(x/log^n x) for every n are equivalent to N(x)=ax+O_n(x/log^n x) for every n. Theorem 3 pins the required C∞ and vertical derivative conditions for the pole-subtracted zeta.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §§1 and 4, Theorems 1 and 3
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A model for checking exact Hardy/Mellin boundary hypotheses. Sectorial smoothness without the specified vertical control is not a substitute for a boundary derivative estimate; these remain Re s≥1 statements.
title: On General Prime Number Theorems with Remainder

main_result: Under Axiom A, one specified zero β₀>θ forces |ψ(x)−x|≥(1−ε)x^β₀/|ρ₀| arbitrarily far out, with factor π/2−ε if γ₀≠0. A constructed model gives near-sharpness in the indicated β₀,r regime.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 Theorems 2–3
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Tests the distinction between detecting an off-line zero through a signed arithmetic witness and obtaining a global norm lower bound. The existence of large subsequence values is not uniform phase recovery or a finite-range estimate.
title: Oscillation of the remainder term in the prime number theorem of Beurling, "caused by a given zeta-zero"

main_result: A power-saving ψ(x)=x+Oε(x^(α+ε)) implies continuation with a simple pole at 1 and zero-freeness on Re s>α. Conversely continuation and zero-freeness yield the same error given uniform subpower growth of the logarithmic derivative in smaller half-planes.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §2.1 Theorem 2.1 and §2.2 Theorem 2.2
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Precisely locates a missing control in transferring zero-free contours to Beurling prime sums. Close real norms are possible, and omitting the log-derivative growth hypothesis would overstate the converse.
title: Beurling Zeta Functions, Generalised Primes, and Fractal Membranes

main_result: Axiom A and a zero-free region Re s>1−η(|t|) yield Δ_P(x)=O(x exp(−(1−ε)ωη(x))), where ωη(x)=inf_{t≥1}(η(t)log x+log t). Infinitely many zeros in that region with η(e^v) convex give the stated Ω counterpart with 1+ε.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 equations (11)–(12) and Theorems 5–6
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A forward/inverse transfer that preserves rather than hides the regularity hypothesis on the boundary. It bounds the order of prime error, without identifying a particular line zero or uniform zero-phase coefficients.
title: The method of Pintz for the Ingham question about the connection of distribution of ζ-zeros and order of the error in the PNT in the Beurling context

main_result: Under Axiom A alone the count at σ>(1+θ)/2 satisfies N(σ,T)≤1000(A+κ)^4 T^(12(1−σ)/(1−θ))(log T)^5/[(1−θ)^3(1−σ)^4] beyond an explicitly parameter-dependent threshold.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §2 Theorem 1, equation (12)
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Supplies a checkable right-slab tail count without an approximate functional equation. It is numerically weaker than later exponents and is not a local derivative sum or a zero-free conclusion.
title: The Carlson-type zero-density theorem for the Beurling zeta function

main_result: For a slowly decreasing function supported on the positive half-line with convergent Laplace transform, local pseudofunction boundary behavior of the remainder after specified poles and log powers yields explicit linear, oscillatory and power-log asymptotic terms plus o(1).
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 Theorem 1.3(i) and §2 definitions
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A candidate transfer from Mellin singularities to real arithmetic asymptotics. Requires the one-sided slowly-decreasing premise and the distributional boundary remainder; sharp pole models or analytic continuation alone do not check either.
title: Complex Tauberian theorems for Laplace transforms with local pseudofunction boundary behavior

main_result: Unweighted fixed-shift correlations are structured in logarithmic scale mean, allowing a twisted character n^{it} in the obstruction. Odd-order and binary Chowla for distinct fixed shifts hold outside a set of logarithmic density zero.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 Theorem 1.7 and Corollaries 1.13–1.14
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Tracks the precise loss in switching from weighted correlations to ordinary averages. A logarithmically negligible scale set can still contain every chosen approximation scale, so deterministic finite-N array control requires a different argument.
title: The structure of correlations of multiplicative functions at almost all scales, with applications to the Chowla and Elliott conjectures

main_result: For fixed κ and multiplicative f in C(κ), whose logarithmic-derivative coefficients are bounded by κΛ, a weighted integral of the maximum of F(1+σ+it)/(1+σ+it) controls Σf(n). Corollary 1.2 gives the (1+M)e^−M suppression from the single-line maximum.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, and Theorem 1.3
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: An exact near-one-line bridge between phase selection and arithmetic sums akin to the Dong localization. Verifying the C(κ) bound and near-one-line maximum is essential, and neither yields critical-line derivative norm control automatically.
title: A new proof of Halász's Theorem, and its consequences

main_result: For admissible independent affine forms and g₁,g₂∈{μ,λ}, claims an effective logarithmic two-point bound ε log ω for x≥ω≥exp₄(CBε^−2), with B from the coefficients. This is a source-stated arXiv theorem.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 Definition 1.1 and Theorems 1.2–1.3
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Useful benchmark for the cost of a genuinely uniform window estimate. Even on its source-stated hypotheses the tower threshold is not a practical finite-N certificate and controls a scalar two-point correlation, not adaptive weighted Gram errors.
title: Effective logarithmic two-point Chowla bounds in every window

main_result: For a zero-topological-entropy system with at most countably many ergodic invariant measures, every orbit's continuous observable has zero logarithmically averaged Möbius and Liouville correlation.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §§1–2, Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 1.6
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: The framework could handle a fixed deterministic test sequence only after constructing its dynamical model and checking the entropy and ergodic-measure hypotheses. It has no bound on growing families of truncation test vectors.
title: The logarithmic Sarnak conjecture for ergodic weights

main_result: For bounded multiplicative functions a joint logarithmic Furstenberg system is a factor of a system with no irrational spectrum and nilsystem–Bernoulli ergodic components. Theorem 1.3 gives orthogonality to suitable zero-entropy, totally ergodic logarithmic test systems.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 Theorems 1.3 and 1.5
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A test for when a deterministic sequence has the kind of irrational phase or ergodicity needed for correlation arguments. These sequence-shift factors are distinct from the compact group indexed by rational logarithms in the zero-tail result.
title: Furstenberg systems of bounded multiplicative functions and applications

main_result: Bounded aperiodic multiplicative functions, meaning zero mean on each infinite arithmetic progression, have vanishing U^s[N] for every fixed s≥2, by a decomposition into a structured component and a uniform component.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §§1–2, Theorems 1.1 and 2.5
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Explains how to handle a fixed-complexity nilsequence test on integer inputs. The existing rational-log Fourier inverse problem does not provide a nilsequence realization or complexity uniformity, so this is not an automatic coefficient bound.
title: Higher order Fourier analysis of multiplicative functions and applications

main_result: When a bounded sequence's distinct-prime dilation correlations sum to o(x) for every fixed pair, it is asymptotically orthogonal to indicators of sets in the three specified multiplicative level-set classes. Counterexample limits arbitrary level sets.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 Theorem A, Definitions 1.3 and Corollary B
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: The dossier's dilations make this an exact possible bridge if the p,q tests can be proved for the concrete sequence. A bound on original inner products without the dilated pair correlations does not verify the criterion.
source_locator: §1 Theorem A, Definitions 1.3 and Corollary B
title: A generalization of Kátai's orthogonality criterion with applications

main_result: For the enveloping-sieve weight β_R of a product of admissible integer linear forms, 1≪R≪N^(1/10) and 1<q<2, a finite cyclic Fourier transform satisfies a weighted L² bound from ℓ^q with constants in q and form count.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §§3–4, Propositions 3.1, 4.1 and 4.2
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Controls additive frequencies for a prime-support majorant. Transferring to t log n requires an explicit finite-frequency embedding and multiplicative collision bound; an additive majorant cannot be silently used in the tapered Mellin Gram matrix.
title: Restriction theory of the Selberg sieve, with applications

main_result: For T^(2/3+ε)≤H≤T the integral of E*(t)^2, the squared difference between the zeta second-moment error and a modified divisor error, is ≫H T^(1/3)log³T. Theorem 2 bounds the integrated residual R in specified ranges.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §1 equations (1.2), (1.3), and Theorems 1–2
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A sharp warning about treating local continuous ζ mean-square errors as flat in dyadic Hardy bounds. E* is an error observable, not the derivative zero measure, and the lower bound excludes rough extrapolation of the smooth main term.
title: On some mean square estimates for the zeta-function in short intervals

main_result: For n≥3, nonvanishing Wronskian of the listed third derivatives and macroscopically separated index intervals yield a multilinear moment bound at p=2(n+1)/(n−1), with a coefficient form. Spacing-count estimates are proved only in stated δ-ranges.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §3 Theorem 1 and Remark (i), §4 Theorem 9
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: Suggests a way to bound off-diagonal frequency collisions after validating a precise phase-curve lift. The multilinear separation and δ regimes are substantive and cannot be read as a generic cluster bound near coincident zero ordinates.
title: Decoupling inequalities and some mean-value theorems

main_result: For fixed real α≠0,1 and M≥2, the number of quadruples of integers in (M,2M] with |m₁^α+m₂^α−m₃^α−m₄^α|≤δM^α is ≪α,ε M^(2+ε)+δM^(4+ε) for δ>0.
read_scope: Targeted reading. §5 Theorem 2 and equations (5.1)–(5.2)
result_status: Source-stated; no transfer to the ordinary critical-line problem is claimed.
selection_reason: A precise input to moment calculations with a curved monomial frequency. It does not automatically bound log-product collisions by α→0, because the exponent is fixed and the constants and normalization would need uniform control as curvature degenerates.
title: Three-dimensional exponential sums with monomials
venue: Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik

main_result: For the microscopic periodization of a Schwartz test f, Theorem 1 gives convergence of the first m ordinary Haar U(N) moments to Gaussian moments when supp(f̂) ⊆ [−2/m,2/m], with mean ∫f and variance ∫min(|u|,1)|f̂(u)|²du for real f. Theorem 2 takes even real f and gives the corresponding support windows [−1/m,1/m] for Sp(N), with N even, and (−1/m,1/m) for SO(N). Theorem 3 gives exact mixed trace moments under the separate total index bounds N+1 and N−1. Theorem 7 attributes the balanced Fourier cumulant estimate to Soshnikov.
read_scope: Targeted theorem and cumulant passages of the journal, compared to arXiv v1. Whole proofs unextracted.
result_status: Recorded primary theorem statements and their Fourier-window scope; no full proof or derivative-rooted transfer claimed.
selection_reason: Classical ordinary-Haar antecedent for finite Fourier-support moment windows. The derivative-rooted rank-two correction requires a separate argument.
source_locator: Printed pp. 2919–2922, introduction and Theorems 1–3; p. 2926, Theorem 7
title: Mock-Gaussian behaviour for linear statistics of classical compact groups
transfer_hypothesis: Classical ordinary-Haar antecedent for finite Fourier-support moment windows. The derivative-rooted rank-two correction requires a separate argument.
venue: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General 36(12), 2919–2932
version: 2003 journal typeset article in author-hosted PDF with one unnumbered provider cover, 15 PDF pages

main_result: With real even f, smooth compact Fourier transform of strict radius sigma, m sigma/2<a and H=T^a, 0<a≤1, the oscillatory prime part has its finite Gaussian window for nonnegative unit-mass bandlimited w. The full statistic has the stated finite Gaussian moments if ∫f=0 or ∫w log^m(2+|u|)<infinity. The literal printed weight class alone is too broad.
read_scope: Complete four-page journal pinned and independently reconstructed; the separate nine-page arXiv v1 was also checked. The original oscillatory moment theorem survives the printed class. The full statistic needs the documented logarithmic-moment alternative and additive comparison.
result_status: Source-stated theorem. The literal weight-tail question and a Schwartz-weight qualification are pending independent director adjudication, not a verified source error.
scope_qualification: The cited note gives a translated band-limited density mixture with divergent log moment under the literally listed weight conditions and presents a sufficient Schwartz setting. Preserve this as an audit candidate separate from the source rendering.
selection_reason: The explicit formula contains the same prime logarithmic frequency but the theorem uses a different sampling law and smooth cutoff.
source_locator: Printed pp. 668–670, Theorem 1.1, Lemmas 2.1–2.2, Proposition 2.3 and (2)–(6); title p. 667
title: Linear statistics for zeros of Riemann’s zeta function

main_result: Propositions 8–9 give the polynomial-normal density/characteristic function equivalence under the normalized-density or actual-characteristic-function premise, with real location b and symmetric positive-definite precision A. The forward direction transforms a degree-2l polynomial times the nonsingular Gaussian density to a degree-2l polynomial times exp(ibtᵀ−tA⁻¹tᵀ/2). The converse assumes this product is a characteristic function and identifies its polynomial-normal density by Fourier uniqueness. Arbitrary polynomial factors need not give positive-definite transforms.
read_scope: Targeted source reading of the definition and transform equivalence. Main decomposition proof unextracted.
result_status: Targeted primary-source confirmation of the transform equivalence. Main decomposition theorem not audited.
selection_reason: Standard transform antecedent for testing a formal arithmetic Gaussian-polynomial continuation for positivity. Positive definiteness is a hypothesis of the converse.
source_locator: Printed pp. 511–512 and 520–522, definition and Propositions 8–9
title: Composition and Decomposition of Multidimensional Polynomial-Normal Distribution
transfer_hypothesis: Standard transform antecedent for testing a formal arithmetic Gaussian-polynomial continuation for positivity. Positive definiteness is a hypothesis of the converse.
venue: Journal of Mathematical Sciences, The University of Tokyo 14(4), 511–530

main_result: For the total zero count of Riemann’s completed xi as a function of t, the opening states an additive O(log T) bound about (T/(2π))log(T/(2π))−T/(2π) for T>28.558, sharpening the additive O(log² T) bound recalled from the same author’s 1895 p. 266. The count is not a count of critical-line zeros alone.
read_scope: Complete original German article, nineteen printed pages plus archive cover, read and reconstructed by the historical agent. Adjacent-argument kernel, one-sided maximum, multiplicities and endpoints independently checked at their source passages. Original decimal bound retained as published rather than fully recertified; no whole-work Level 2/3 promotion.
result_status: Primary theorem statement only; no whole-proof or exact boundary convention claim.
selection_reason: Primary source of the sharper logarithmic error scale for the classical total zero count, separating the 1859 sketch, 1895 count and 1905 improvement.
source_locator: Printed p. 1 (PDF p. 2), opening theorem and footnote citing the 1895 count on p. 266
title: Zur Verteilung der Nullstellen der Riemannschen Funktion ξ(t)
transfer_hypothesis: Classical total zero count supplies an analytic input for local height-ordered estimates. It does not establish the number of critical-line zeros or RH.
version: 1905 original German journal scan, GDZ PPN235181684_0060, LOG_0007; one provider cover followed by printed pp. 1–19
